newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria produced 400,000 bales of cotton in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria produced 400,000 bales of cotton in 1996.

text.p: Nigeria's cotton production rose to 400,000 bales from 150,000 bales in the previous year, the national news agency reported on Thursday.

The News Agency of Nigeria quoted Walid Jibrin, chairman of the Cotton Revolving Fund Committee, as saying in Abuja that the increase was enhanced by the 54 million naira given it by the military government to boost cotton production.
"The money from the government was added to the 4.5 million naira jointly contributed by the textiles manufacturers in the country for the same purpose," Jibrin said.

He said he doubted if production levels of the commodity would rise this year as farmers now exported the commodity for higher prices because the government had removed textiles from its import prohibition list.
In January, government announced in its fiscal budget that textiles could now be imported into the country.
Cotton is now sold by local farmers at 180 naira per kilogramme, compared to 90 naira last year, Jibrin said.
